This page summarizes key results from the blue, fin, and sei whale
analyses conducted using drifting acoustic recorder data collected during
the 2024 California Current Cetacean and Ecosystem Assessment Survey
(CalCurCEAS). Complete data products and supporting outputs are available
in the project repository.

## Validated hourly occurrence

Summary of manually validated hourly occurrence of blue, fin, and sei
whales across geographic zones.

\[Key figure/table goes here\]

## Detector performance on novel CalCurCEAS data

Performance of the final DeepAcoustics TinyYOLO detector was evaluated
using manually annotated novel CalCurCEAS recordings. Automated
call-level analyses were restricted to call types meeting the specified
performance criterion.

\[Compact performance figure or table goes here\]

## Relative automated call activity

For call types with sufficient detector performance, automated detections
were summarized relative to acoustic recording effort to characterize
variation in call activity among geographic zones.

\[Key figure/table goes here\]

## Environmental context

Exploratory comparisons were used to describe the environmental
conditions associated with call-positive and call-negative hours.
These analyses are descriptive and were not intended as formal habitat
models.

\[Optional compact figure or short summary\]

## Data products

Supporting datasets, tables, figures, model files, and analysis outputs
used for the baleen whale analyses are available in the GitHub repository.
